text:
jamal: Heads-up — running nsys traces on the dedicated cluster after the node driver bump and seeing intermittent attach failures + a perf regression on kv-cache hotpath.

alex: error logs?

jamal: paste from failed trace: `CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED (11)`, then `nsys: failed to attach to process: permission denied`. Happening in our rootless container jobs.

rachel: rootless + new driver rings a bell. Which driver and nsys versions?

jamal: nodes are on driver 535.86, CUDA 12.2. nsys shipped in our infra image is 2023.11. Tried nvprof too — nvprof runs but gives noisy kernel timeline and misses some kernels due to driver mismatch.

sam: for permission denied, did you see CAP_SYS_ADMIN / uid map issues? rootless containers need uidmap + SYS_PTRACE for attach.

jamal: checked. The uidmap is fine; container lacks CAP_SYS_ADMIN by design. But older nsys used CUPTI in a way that can attach without extra caps; newer nsys triggers a driver codepath requiring extra perms.

maria: can we repro outside container on baremetal? helps isolate kernel vs container permission.

jamal: repro on a bare machine works but shows weird kernel selection pattern: our timeline shows repeated small kernels instead of the fused attention kernel — throughput drops ~18% when KV cache warms.

alex: do you have the kernel names?

jamal: nvprof/ perfetto slices show heavy activity in `scaled_dot_product_attention` and `kv_cache_memcpy` interleaving. Expected a single `multi_head_attention_fused` large kernel. Looks like runtime picked different kernels mid-sequence (kernel switching).

rachel: that smells like the runtime picking a quantized-friendly kernel vs fp16-fused one based on sequence length heuristic. If batching heuristic misclassifies, we could get smaller kernels and more launches -> higher overhead.

sam: also KV cache memcpy spikes indicate cache eviction/rehydration. Could be kvcache placement + pinned memory fallback causing copies.

jamal: timeline snippet (trimmed):
```
[0.00s] multi_head_attention_fused       2.1ms
[0.002s] kv_cache_memcpy                  0.08ms
[0.003s] scaled_dot_product_attention    3.6ms
[0.006s] kv_cache_memcpy                  0.09ms
[... repeated pattern ...]
```

maria: can you share nsys command you used?

jamal: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=none --output=trace-nodeA ns-launch --run ./serve-bench --profile`. Also tried `nsys attach --target 1234` which fails with the CUPTI error.

alex: two things to try: (1) run nsys from host (not in container) to avoid attach perms, (2) pin runtime to previous driver/kernel selection heuristic and re-run to confirm kernel choice is the cause.

rachel: quick sanity check: compare kernel symbol mangles between driver versions. sometimes the symbol exported for fused kernel changes and our kernel selector falls back.

sam: I also saw an issue where nsys filters certain small kernels when built against older CUPTI headers — that could explain missing fused kernel in traces.

jamal: workaround for attach: run with `--no-cupti`? There's an env `NSYS_DISABLE_CUPTI_ATTACH=1` we tried; it allows profiling but loses some activity. For the perf regression debug we need full timeline.

maria: If we can repro the kernel switching deterministically: capture two traces (driver old vs new) on same load and diff the kernel list. That will show if selector changed.

alex: also try `LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcupti.so` from host to force the CUPTI we want. But be careful with ABI mismatches.

rachel: Regarding batching heuristics, we should log the runtime decision path (sequence length, batch size, quantization flag) to trace logs when a kernel choice is made. Add a short-lived flag to print the reason for each kernel selection.

jamal: good idea — adding `RT_KERNEL_DEBUG=1` prints: `selected_kernel=fp16_unfused reason=batch_small shard=1`. That explains the switch for mid-batch length changes.

sam: So root cause appears twofold: (A) CUPTI/nsys attach behavior changed after driver bump causing friction with rootless profiling, and (B) our kernel selector heuristic misfires for certain mixed-length batches causing unfused kernels + extra KV memcpy.

maria: action items?

jamal: I'll: 1) collect paired traces old-driver vs new-driver (host-level nsys to avoid attach perms), 2) add selective kernel-selection debug logging and run with representative traffic, 3) capture memory ops to confirm kvcache memcpy source/dest.

alex: I'll try forcing CUPTI version on a staging node and see if `nsys attach` recovers. If it's an unavoidable driver change we may need to update our tracing images and guidance for rootless customers.

rachel: I'll file a tiny regression ticket to tweak batching heuristic (prefer fused kernel when kv-cache hits > threshold).

sam: ping me when you have traces; I can run perfetto-based postproc to produce flamegraphs and a kernel diff.

trace-bot: note created — perf/infra/1967890123: added initial trace artifacts checklist and attach reproducibility steps.

jamal: thanks folks. I'll push the two traces to the ticket in the next hour. :thumbsup:
